In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ACP is a highly dynamic molecule, which can accommodate all intermediates in the biosynthesis of fatty acids.
the ACP is an efficient molecular switch that controls the direction of fatty acid biosynthetic intermediates through the FAS.
the acyl chain transfer in a FAS is programmed and not diffusion controlled.

ACP is a key player in the recognition of intermediates and in the regulation of FAS activity.
the ACP is a key player in the recognition of intermediates over a complete cycle in fatty acid biosyntheses.

ACPs have the potential to recognize and distinguish between all intermediates in fatty acid biosyntheses, and this recognition is a programmed process that ensures effective transfer between the enzymes of the fatty acid synthesis pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ACP is an essential component of the fatty acid synthase and that the ACP plays a critical role in directing and maintaining the flow of intermediates during fatty acid biosynthesis by the FAS.
acyl transfer in FAS is a programmed, not random, process.
the ACP has evolved to recognize the intermediates in a programmed fashion, thus providing a molecular basis for the ordered action of FAS.
